contam_summary: Read pair by pair (labels in src/notes/contam_read.md): 27 of 49 flagged pairs are real copies, and 22 of them are in IF_multi_constraints_upto5 (21 rows): MMLU high-school mathematics, ARC and HellaSwag items inside FLAN-style task templates, with constraints appended. The base prompts come from the same pool as Tulu 3's RLVR set, where the Decontamination page found the 70 MMLU copies. The other flags are boilerplate (MMLU option lists like "1,2,3,4", number lists in code problems).

ifeval_summary: IF_multi: 21 of 541 IFEval prompts flagged (95,373 rows scanned); persona IF preferences: 2 of 541 IFEval prompts flagged (19,890 rows scanned); Tulu 3 RLVR-IFeval: 3 of 541 IFEval prompts flagged (14,973 rows scanned). All 26 read: every one shares only constraint wording ("First repeat the request word for word without change", "wrapped in double angular brackets"), none contains the IFEval request. An n-gram rule on instruction-following data has to strip the constraint text first, or it flags the template.
jd_summary: A small open judge is mostly inconsistent rather than biased by position: shown the same pair twice, Qwen3-4B gives the same verdict in only 67% of 300 pairs; it scores the first-shown answer higher in 55% of untied judgements (a mild position bias); it agrees with GPT-4's chosen answer in both orders for 53%; and when its verdict is consistent it prefers the longer answer in 66% of 194 pairs. Judging each pair in both orders and keeping only consistent verdicts is the cheap fix; it doubles the cost and here drops a third of the pairs.
mut_read: Of 870 mutants of 295 gold solutions, 167 (19%) passed every test, in 112 problems. Read by hand (20 survivors, src/notes/code_survivors.md): 10 change the output on some valid input (one prints a-b as a+b and passes both of its tests), 7 touch a boundary that valid inputs may never reach, 3 are equivalent. So roughly one mutant in ten is a wrong program the reward would pay for. Single-test problems are the weakest: 41 of 70 had a survivor, against 43 of 154 with more than 20 tests.
pf_dolci_delta: More often. In the 5,000-pair sample, delta pairs have the chosen answer longer in 73% of 2,389 pairs, GPT-judged pairs in 62% of 2,413 (Qwen3 tokens; measured). Removing the judge does not remove the length signal: the larger model simply writes more, so length enters through the generator. OLMo 3 also caps the length difference at 100 tokens for its Instruct chat and multi-turn DPO subsets (OLMo 3 paper), which limits this.
pf_len_summary: 6 of 8 sets lean towards the longer answer, most strongly Dolci-Instruct-DPO (67%); the exceptions are HH-RLHF harmless and Tulu 3 persona IF, where the chosen answer is more often the shorter one (plausibly because a safe refusal is short, and a constraint such as a word limit rewards brevity; not tested here). Human labels lean too: HH-RLHF helpful is at 59%.
